changes.before: val gives a value a reusable name.
changes.after: Use val to give a value a name you can use again.

before: Before this: Kotlin lesson 1, Display text. You will reuse the earlier display function and value names.
A variable is a name you can use to refer to a value. A value is an individual piece of information.
val topic = "Stars" introduces topic and assigns text to it. Kotlin infers the String type: the kind of value is text.
println(topic) reads the named value. println("topic") would display the literal word topic instead. val does not allow reassigning this variable.

Complete example to read, not an in-app run:
```kotlin
fun main() {
    val topic = "Stars"
    println(topic)
}
```

Expected output from this example, explained rather than executed here:
```text
Stars
```
after: A value is one piece of information, such as text or a number.
A variable gives a value a name. You can use that name later to read the value.
In `val topic = "Stars"`, `topic` is the name and `"Stars"` is its value. The `=` gives the starting value. The word `val` means you cannot assign a different value to this name later.
Use `topic` without quotes to read its value. Put a word in quotes when you want that exact word as text.

Follow the example one line at a time.
```kotlin
fun main() {
    val topic = "Stars"
    println(topic)
}
```
The screen shows `Stars`. The name `topic` leads to that text.
